reuse.why: All six link handlers share one assertNotLinkedElsewhere guard and the new handler reuses findOrCreateBank/syncAccount/handleSyncResponse, but the takeover re-writes unlinkAccount's field reset and the Fintegra link/download are copies of the Pluggy link and Akahu download.

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount is a near-verbatim copy of linkPluggyAiAccount, downloadFintegraTransactions copies downloadAkahuTransactions (plus a file-id header), and the detach loop repeats unlinkAccount's db.updateAccount field list.

placement.why: Guard next to the link handlers in accounts/app.ts, download and balance rule in sync.ts, endpoint in server-config.ts, following the tree's per-provider layout; an 'assert' that also mutates other accounts is an odd home for the takeover.

scope.why: Limited to the four steps plus release notes; the guard's provider parameter is a plain string rather than the existing sync-source type.

maintainability.why: One guard for every provider is good, but it has grown a closed-account check and a mutating takeover behind an 'assert' name, and every new provider adds another ~70-line copy; no tests accompany the change.

bypasses_abstraction.where: assertNotLinkedElsewhere clears the previous holder with its own db.updateAccount field list instead of sharing the reset with unlinkAccount

disguised_duplication.where: The copies (Fintegra link vs Pluggy link, Fintegra download vs Akahu download, unlink reset) are open near-verbatim copies.

abstraction_drift.where: assertNotLinkedElsewhere in accounts/app.ts gains replaceExistingLink, the closed upgrading-account branch and the unlink-previous-holders branch; all six provider link handlers call it
